svg.title: Which design to start from
svg.desc: Seven rows, each a situation, the design to start from, and what this experiment showed. The history fits in the prompt: no memory; the whole history, or a keyword search over the raw turns with their dates. A small profile that people can read and correct: textual memory, one rewrite per session. Too many facts for one profile: a fact store with search, with dates written and shown. Earlier values or links between people and things matter: a dated graph. The agent should decide what to keep: an agent that edits its memory, told when to write, how to date and what to do with the old value. Answers depend on what the user implies: a background reasoner, read as dated conclusions. In every case: read what the system stored.
svg.text: Which design to start from
Defaults by situation, not a ranking. Each row says what this experiment showed about the design.
IF
START WITH
IN THIS EXPERIMENT
The history fits in the prompt
No memory: the whole history, or a keyword
search over the raw turns with their dates
Search over raw turns scored highest (97%) at
the lowest cost ($0.002 per question); it writes
nothing, so it cannot lose an update.
A person should be able to read
and correct the memory
Textual memory: one profile, rewritten after
each session
93%. It kept the old value as current in only 9%
of questions; its write cost grew 13 times on the
whole history.
Too many facts for one profile
A fact store with search (Mem0), with the
conversation's dates written into the facts and
shown at read time
84%. Old and new values were both kept; when
both reached the answering model with their
dates, it answered 41 of 45 correctly.
Earlier values, or links between
people and things, matter
A dated graph (Graphiti), fed one message at a
time
Answered all 8 questions about an earlier value,
at about 30 times the cost of textual memory and
with a graph database to run.
The agent itself should decide
what to keep
An agent that edits its memory (Letta), told
when to write, how to date and what to do
with the old value
69% as shipped; 90% with three lines in its
persona that say exactly that.
Answers depend on what the
user implies
A background reasoner (Honcho), read as a
list of dated conclusions
93% as a dated list; 87% through its chat agent,
which declined to choose between two dated
values.
In every case
Read what the system stored, not only its
score
Two configurations scored 18% and 58% with no
error anywhere, until the stored memory was
read.
agent-memory-eval: LongMemEval knowledge-update questions, 67 per configuration
